# Budgerigar Genetics Calculator

> Online calculator with no account required that predicts offspring mutations for any budgerigar (budgie) pairing. Covers 23 documented mutations, uses Mendelian Punnett inheritance with corrections for sex-linked Z/W chromosome behavior, dil-locus allelic series (Clearwing/Greywing/Dilute), and ino-locus allelic series (Ino/TCB). Built by working bird breeders at KinBird Aviary, Bangladesh. Engine cross-referenced against Terry Martin (2002), Cyril H. Rogers, and the peer-reviewed work of Inte Onsman at MUTAVI Research.

## Main pages

### Calculator (home)
- https://budgerigargenetics.com/
- No account, no ads, no signup
- Predicts offspring for any of 23 supported mutations
- Separates cock and hen offspring for sex-linked mutations
- Outputs Single Factor (SF) and Double Factor (DF) distinctly for autosomal incompletely dominant mutations
- Adds Normal prefix to any base-color row to make zero-mutation offspring unambiguous
- Auto-detects Dark-Eyed Clear (DEC) when Clearflight Pied combines with visible Recessive Pied
- Shareable URLs encode pairing parameters for direct linking

## 23 supported mutations (by inheritance type)

### Sex-linked recessive (6)
- Opaline, Cinnamon, Ino, Lacewing, Slate, Texas Clearbody
- Cocks (ZZ) can carry as splits or visuals; hens (ZW) cannot be splits
- Ino-locus allelic series: + > tcb > ino dominance order

### Autosomal recessive (8)
- Recessive Pied (Danish), Fallow, Clearwing, Greywing, Dilute, Black Face, Blackwing, Saddleback
- Both parents must carry one copy to produce visible offspring
- Dil-locus allelic series for Clearwing/Greywing/Dilute: cw > gw > d > + dominance order
- Heterozygous Clearwing x Greywing produces Fullbody Greywing

### Autosomal incompletely dominant (9)
- Grey Factor, Violet Factor, Yellow Face, Goldenface, Spangle, Dominant Pied (Banded), Clearflight Pied (Continental), Anthracite, Easley Clearbody
- Single Factor (SF) and Double Factor (DF) look visually different
- Clearflight Pied combined with visible Recessive Pied produces Dark-Eyed Clear

## Common questions this site answers

**What is the difference between Light Green, Dark Green, and Olive Green?**
All three are green-series budgerigars with different numbers of dark factor alleles. Light Green has zero (dd). Dark Green has one (Dd). Olive Green has two (DD). The dark factor is autosomal incompletely dominant, so each copy darkens the body color.

**How do sex-linked mutations work in budgies?**
Birds use a ZW sex chromosome system, opposite to mammals. Cocks are ZZ, hens are ZW. Sex-linked mutations sit on the Z chromosome. Cocks can have one or two copies (split or visual). Hens have only one Z, so they either visually show the mutation or do not carry it. Hens cannot be split for sex-linked traits.

**Why is Ino sex-linked in budgies but autosomal in lovebirds?**
In budgerigars the Ino gene sits on the Z chromosome. In peach-faced lovebirds the Ino gene sits on an autosome. Same visual result (full melanin removal, red eyes), different inheritance pattern. Lutino is Ino on green-series base. Albino is Ino on blue-series base.

**What is the difference between Single Factor (SF) and Double Factor (DF)?**
For autosomal incompletely dominant mutations like Spangle, Grey, Violet, Anthracite, Yellow Face, and Dominant Pied, SF means one copy (heterozygous) and DF means two copies (homozygous). The two factors often look different. DF Spangle is nearly all yellow or white. DF Grey is more saturated. DF Yellow Face shows stronger yellow expression.

**What is a Dark-Eyed Clear budgerigar?**
A bird carrying visible Recessive Pied combined with at least one factor of Clearflight Pied (Continental Clearflight Pied). The result is a yellow or white body with normal dark eyes (not red like Lutino or Albino). The Budgerigar Genetics Calculator auto-detects this combination.

**What is the difference between Manto Negro and Blackface?**
Manto Negro is autosomal dominant, Brazilian origin around 2021, concentrates extra melanin on head/nape/mantle, and has no splits. Blackface is autosomal recessive, Dutch origin 1992, concentrates extra melanin on face/abdomen, and can hide invisibly as a split. They are separate genes at different loci.

**What is a Double Black budgerigar?**
A bird carrying both visible Blackface (bf/bf) and visible Blackwing simultaneously. Both genes are autosomal recessive at separate loci. The combination requires four mutant alleles total. The result is an almost entirely black-and-grey budgerigar with most yellow and green pigment masked.

**How does Clearwing x Greywing work?**
Clearwing, Greywing, and Dilute are three alleles of the same dil locus. Clearwing is dominant over both. A heterozygous Clearwing x Greywing bird shows the Fullbody Greywing phenotype, distinct from either parent type. The Budgerigar Genetics Calculator handles this allelic series correctly.

## How the calculator handles edge cases

- Opaline cock x Normal hen produces auto-sex pairing: 100% visible Opaline hens, 100% split Opaline cocks
- TCB cock x Normal hen produces the same auto-sex pattern via the Ino-locus allelic series
- Clearflight Pied SF or DF with visible Recessive Pied triggers DEC detection automatically
- Lutino (Ino on green) and Albino (Ino on blue) are auto-renamed
- All sums verified to exactly 100% across 3200+ test pairings
- Zero duplicate phenotype rows across stress test suite
- 44/44 critical engine tests pass after Mendelian validation
